title: Stacks in big blinds
summary: Blinds grow in a tournament: how stack depth changes the plan and what antes do.

bb.text: In a tournament the blinds keep growing, so a stack is measured in **big blinds** (BB), not chips. 20,000 chips at 500/1,000 blinds is 20 BB, and it has to be played as 20 BB, however many chips you started with.

zones.text:
Reference points by stack:
- **40 BB and more**: normal play with opens, 3-bets and postflop.
- **20–40 BB**: fewer flat calls and speculative hands, more 3-bets you can follow with all-in.
- **10–20 BB**: open or **3-bet all-in**; calling opens with small pairs and connectors loses its point, there are no implied odds.
- **Below 10–12 BB**: **push/fold**, all-in or fold.

ante.text: The **ante** grows the pot before anyone acts. With a big blind ante (the usual format) the pot already holds 2.5 BB: 0.5 + 1 + 1. Stealing it pays more, so opens get wider and smaller, **2–2.2 BB**. The big blind defends wider too: the pot gives it great pot odds.

q-bb.q: Blinds 1,000/2,000, you have 30,000 chips. How many big blinds is that?
q-bb.explain: 30,000 / 2,000 = 15 BB: time to think about 3-bet all-ins.

t1.q: Why are tournament stacks measured in big blinds?
options: Blinds grow, and what matters is how many bets you have left
Chips mean nothing in a tournament
t1.explain: The same chips are a deep stack early and a short one later.

t2.q: How do antes change the game?
options: The pot is bigger: opens get wider and smaller
Only premium hands can be played
t2.explain: More money in the pot makes every steal more profitable.

t3.q: At about what stack does push/fold usually start?
t3.explain: Below 10–12 BB a normal open leaves no good answer to a 3-bet.
